# Stakeholder Interview Notes (FICTIONAL - EA team, September 2026)

## Annelies Claes - COO, programme sponsor
- "Customers see three companies. By the end of 2028 they should see one Acme."
- No migrations during the peak season.
- Wants a clear go/no-go per business unit.

## Marc Dubois - CFO
- Run cost of the three portals (EUR 1.31M) must drop by at least 35%.
- Payback within 4 years. Discovery budget EUR 350,000 approved; total envelope EUR 4-6M indicative.
- Does not want to renew TrackBox for another 3 years if it can be avoided.

## Sofie Peeters - CIO
- Liferay hosting ends June 2027: Portal B is the first forced move.
- Prefers a SaaS or low-code platform on Azure over another custom build.
- Wants one customer identity platform for all channels.

## Nathalie Lambert - Head of Customer Service
- 410,000 contacts per year; 31% are "where is my shipment?".
- Agents switch between three portals and two CRMs. Average handling time 7 min 40 s; first-contact resolution 64%.
- Customers with several contracts get three invoice layouts and call to ask which one is right.

## Pieter Janssens - CISO
- Portal A has no MFA and was hit by credential stuffing in February 2025.
- NIS2: Acme is an important entity; CyFun level Important by end 2027.
- Wants one hardened login and central security logging.

## Isabelle Martin - DPO
- 140 data subject requests per year, answered in 41 days on average (legal limit: one month). The data sits in three portals and two CRMs.
- TrackBox support access from outside the EU is an open finding.
- Agents must not see more personal data than the contact needs.

## Koen De Smet (A), Julie Leclercq (B), Tom Wouters (C) - portal owners
- Fear losing features their customers rely on: A the returns flow, B the EDI order upload, C the temperature alerts and certificates.
- Pharma customers require audit-proof temperature records: non-negotiable for Tom.
- All three want usage data before deciding what can be dropped.
